structured_output.existing_resolution_path: One genuine, authorized path exists, but it is membership-level eviction, not per-source resolution. Creator issues `acl` revoke of the held author, closes, adopts, then issues `acl` grant and closes again (existing public `issue()` surface, existing creator authority). The returning author gets a new `admissionEpoch` (design.md ACL transition law; test `sameKeyReentry` asserts `[writer.author, 4, null]` at tests/phase-6b-d110c-0c1f5b-integration-red.test.ts:1448). On the next reopen its old rows classify `old-incarnation` (packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:4944-4955) and are skipped by the outbox (v3-live.ts:7044-7058) because `openProgressSources` only ever contains entries carrying `replacementProgress` (v3-live.ts:8822-8826) and a `manual-review` entry can never carry progress (packages/issuance-store/src/contract.ts:457). `writeMergedSettlementPlan` rebuilds entries only from the returned sources (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2931-2953), so the held entry is dropped at merge, the prune gate releases (packages/issuance-store/src/maintenance.ts:113-124), the plan becomes empty and the fence issues (RED case 7 `F5B_C07_EMPTY_PLAN_STILL_FENCES`). The store permits the entry to disappear: `assertSettlementPlanProgressTransition` (contract.ts:546-593) constrains only progress-bearing or already-linked entries. Limits that make it unsuitable as case 11's promised resolver: it is author-wide (every held entry dies at once, reviewed or not), it discards the held content (recoverable only by the application re-issuing it as fresh operations, as the design already licenses), it requires creator ACL authority plus two closes, it is user-visible membership churn (kick + re-invite), and it restores only the roles the operator remembers to re-grant. It resolves the plan by voiding it, not by dispositioning the reviewed source.

Nothing in the construction itself is unsound — the fence/plan/checkpoint semantics, contiguity, prune gate and one-fence-per-epoch bound all hold up under this audit — so the reslice is confined to case 11's obligation and the hold's liveness semantics, not to the settlement design. findings.title: Case 11's resolver does not exist and is unreachable in-session
findings.evidence: design.md:501 promises "resolving the hold later completes the plan". `settlementHold` (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2005-2007) is resolved only by `closeSession()` (:4319), which exists so shutdown can proceed. `drainSettlementOutbox` awaits it inside the lifetime-transition queue (:3158-3163, :3529-3547) and is never re-entered, `V3RoomSession` (:414-431) exposes no resolver, and `writeMergedSettlementPlan` rejects a changed disposition outright (:2941-2943). The parent RED `manualReviewHold` (tests/phase-6b-d110c-0c1f5b-integration-red.test.ts:1505-1554) asserts only durable persistence.
findings.action: Adopt option C: amend design case 11 and the matrix row to the demonstrable statement, and name D.110c-0c1f5b0x as the owner of per-source resolution.

findings.title: Held issue() hangs instead of failing closed, so RED cases 11 and 21 cannot go GREEN
findings.evidence: `issue()` awaits `rebasePromise` (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:4405); under a hold that promise never settles (:3529-3547 -> :3160-3162). Both fixtures assert `rejects.toThrow()` on it — tests/phase-6b-d110c-0c1f5b-integration-red.test.ts:1522 (`F5B_C11_MANUAL_REVIEW_BARRIER`) and :1385-1388 (`F5B_C21_DISPLACED_ACL_HOLDS_BEFORE_FENCE`) — so the call can only settle if something else closes the session; otherwise the fixture deadlocks to the 60s timeout.
findings.action: f5b0w item 1: replace the unresolvable await with a typed settlement-held refusal at `issue()`, keeping the hold itself indefinite and fail-closed.

findings.title: A creator-owned manual-review entry stalls every author, not just its own
findings.evidence: `sealEpoch()` awaits `rebasePromise` (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:4467) and the creator is the only closing authority under `creator-trusted-settlement-v1`; design.md states the creator's own displaced rows take the same plan/fence path (:181-182) while the matrix row (:391) and `F5B_C11_ONLY_HELD_AUTHOR_STALLS` claim only that author stalls — the fixture only ever holds a non-creator writer (tests:1505-1538).
findings.action: f5b0w item 2: decouple the close path from this author's own held drain (matrix rows 15/16 already permit replacements after a close), or state the restriction honestly in the matrix.

findings.title: Store contract has no one-way disposition law; only the room guard stands in for it
findings.evidence: `assertSettlementPlanProgressTransition` (packages/issuance-store/src/contract.ts:546-593) constrains only progress-bearing or already-linked entries, and contract.ts:457 forbids progress on `manual-review` entries, so no branch constrains them. A CAS write may flip `rebase -> manual-review` after `fenceSequence` is durable, permanently re-arming the prune gate (packages/issuance-store/src/maintenance.ts:113-124) and making the entry unlinkable (contract.ts:651). Only examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2941 prevents this today — the exact guard option B would relax.
findings.action: f5b0w item 3: enforce `manual-review -> expire|rebase|transform` one-way, with `sourceDigest` immutability, in the store with conformance vectors.

findings.title: A legitimate policy change fails the session closed rather than refusing typed
findings.evidence: examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2941-2943 throws a bare `TypeError("v3 room settlement plan source differs")`; the throw is caught at :3538-3546, assigned to `terminalFailure` and triggers `shutdown()`. An operator who edits `displacementPolicies` after review therefore bricks that author's session instead of being refused.
findings.action: Whichever option is adopted, make the merge emit a typed refusal (or an explicitly allowed transition); never a session-terminal throw.

findings.title: Option B is action-granular, not per-source
findings.evidence: `settlementDisposition` looks policy up by `action` only (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2915, and again at :3119, :3381, :3442); `displacementPolicies` is `Readonly<Record<string, ...>>` (:360). In a room whose held items are all `message`, one policy flip resolves every held source at once.
findings.action: Do not describe B as per-source review; if the product needs per-source decisions, that is D.110c-0c1f5b0x with a held-source read surface.

findings.title: Migration redirect forces manual-review on every source and would hang session creation
findings.evidence: `settlementDisposition` returns `manual-review` whenever `redirectSource !== undefined` (examples/v3-room/src/index.ts:2927), and the redirect constructor awaits `rebasePromise` (:4153-4160). A migration target carrying any displaced source with intents would never return from `createV3RoomSessionOwned` rather than fail closed. Latent today because the target scope is fresh, but it is the same defect class as the held `issue()` hang.
findings.action: Cover the redirect path in f5b0w item 1 so migration-import debt fails closed with a typed error instead of hanging.
